args.brief: Chapter 3, "The Duplicate." Write it lighter on both counts, since the two readings can hold at once: open the depot workroom in clear morning daylight, with the roller shutters raised and dust visible in the sun, and let the mood lift too — Oren and Lena easier with each other now, small dry jokes, no crisis. Keep Lena's viewpoint, third-person past, precise practical actions. Lena reads the handling note attached to the sample case and asks Suri about the missing second page of the service register. Suri produces a duplicate page from the public records and the three of them read it together; the tension over the disputed delivery eases without being resolved. The case stays sealed and intact — no character opens it or damages it. No physical injury to anyone. End on a definite lighter beat: a workable next check agreed, with the sunlight still on the floor.
